_meta.indication: PREZISTA, co-administered with 100 mg ritonavir and with other antiretroviral agents, is indicated for the treatment of HIV infection in antiretroviral treatment-experienced adult patients, such as those with HIV-1 strains resistant to more than one protease inhibitor.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: TMC114-C213 and TMC114-C202 (pooled), supported by the non-randomized TMC114-C215/C208 analysis
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, controlled trials comparing PREZISTA/rtv 600/100 mg b.i.d. plus an optimized background regimen (OBR) versus a control group receiving investigator-selected PI(s) plus an OBR; randomization stratified by number of PI mutations, screening viral load, and enfuvirtide use.
pivotal_trials.population: Antiretroviral treatment-experienced HIV-1 infected adults with plasma HIV-1 RNA >1000 copies/mL, prior PI, NNRTI and NRTI treatment, and at least one primary PI mutation at screening.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Virologic response at Week 24, defined as a confirmed decrease in plasma HIV-1 RNA viral load of at least 1.0 log10 versus baseline.
pivotal_trials.n: Pooled randomized analysis: PREZISTA/rtv arm N=131, comparator PI arm N=124
pivotal_trials.result: Week 24 virologic responders (>=1 log10 below baseline): 69.5% with PREZISTA/rtv vs 21.0% comparator (with <50 copies/mL: 45.0% vs 12.1%). Mean HIV-1 RNA change -1.89 vs -0.48 log10 copies/mL; mean CD4+ increase 92 vs 17 cells/mm3.

nct_ctgov.title: TMC114-C202: A Study of Safety, Efficacy, and Tolerability of TMC114 and Low Dose Ritonavir in HIV-1 Infected Patients

key_safety: Most common treatment-emergent adverse events (>10%) were diarrhea, nausea, headache, and nasopharyngitis; in the pooled randomized trials diarrhea 19.8% (vs 28.2% comparator), nausea 18.3% (vs 12.9%), headache 15.3% (vs 20.2%), and nasopharyngitis 13.7% (vs 10.5%). Severe skin rash, including erythema multiforme and Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, has been reported; rash of all grades occurred in 7% of subjects.
target_moa: Darunavir is an inhibitor of the HIV-1 protease; it selectively inhibits cleavage of HIV-encoded Gag-Pol polyproteins in infected cells, thereby preventing formation of mature virus particles.

description.text: Fulfilled accelerated approval postmarketing commitments (96-week Phase 2b and 48-week Phase 3 data) for darunavir/ritonavir in treatment-experienced adult HIV patients

citations.quote: This application is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the agreed-upon labeling text and patient labeling. We approved this NDA (21-976/000) under the 21 CFR 314 Subpart H regulations for accelerated approval of new drugs for serious or life-threatening illnesses. Approval of this supplement and NDA 21-976, supplement 007, fulfills your commitments made under 21 CFR 314.510, listed as PMCs 1 and 2 in the June 23, 2006, approval letter:

description.text: Expanded indication to include treatment of HIV in antiretroviral treatment-naïve adults with a new once-daily dosing regimen (two 400 mg tablets with 100 mg ritonavir)

citations.quote: This supplemental new drug application was submitted to expand the indication to include the treatment of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in antiretroviral treatment-naïve adults and to include a new dosing regimen, two 400 mg tablets of PREZISTA once a day, co-administered with 100 mg of ritonavir.

description.text: Added dosing recommendations for HIV-1 infected pediatric patients 6 to less than 18 years of age and two new dosage strengths (75 mg and 150 mg tablets)

citations.quote: This supplemental new drug application was submitted to provide dosing recommendations for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1) infected pediatric patients 6 to less than 18 years of age and to include two new dosage strengths, 75 mg and 150 mg tablets.

description.text: Updated labeling with 96-week data from treatment-experienced and treatment-naive trials to support use for HIV-1 infection

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications provide for updates to the U.S. Package Insert and Patient Package Insert with 96 week data from two trials, one in treatment-experienced patients and one in treatment-naive patients to support the use of PREZISTA® (darunavir) tablets for the treatment of HIV-1 infection.

description.text: Added once-daily 800/100 mg darunavir/ritonavir dosing regimen for treatment-experienced HIV-1 patients with no darunavir resistance-associated substitutions

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new dosing regimen, 800/100 mg darunavir/ritonavir, once daily, in treatment-experienced HIV-1 infected patients with no darunavir resistance associated substitutions based on the results of Study TMC114-C229. The Patient Package Insert was revised to include the new dosing regimen and to provide a more user friendly label to prevent and/or reduce medication errors. In addition, all references to the 300 mg tablets were deleted and Hepatotoxicity and Severe Skin Reactions sections were added to Patient Counseling-Instructions for Use of the Package Insert.

description.text: Updated labeling with 192-week safety and efficacy data from study TMC114-C211 and added rash information when used in combination with raltegravir

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes to update the package insert (PI) with 192-week safety and efficacy data from clinical study TMC114-C211 and update the "What are the possible side effects of PREZISTA?" section of the patient package insert (PPI) with information related to rash when PREZISTA is taken in combination with raltegravir.

description.text: Expanded pediatric indication to include HIV-1-infected patients 3 years of age and older (previously 6 years and older)

description.text: Expanded pediatric indication to include patients 3 years of age and older (previously 6 years and older), including treatment-naïve pediatric patients

citations.quote: PREZISTA, co-administered with ritonavir (PREZISTA/ritonavir), and with other antiretroviral agents, is indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in pediatric patients 3 years of age and older [see Use in Specific Populations (8.4)].
